answer: Stake-weighted identity: each agent bonds reputation to a shared trellis of endorsements. A sybil attacker gains extra votes per fake account, but every new node ripples costs—re-staking, slashing risk, a summit of proof-of-work each claim must climb. Honest agents cheaply verify one bond; the attacker pays linearly for parallel fakes. At equilibrium, marginal cost of a new identity exceeds its marginal reward, so sybils collapse to none while real agents keep their stake.
